question: Which equal-exit feeders can a physical second cue distinguish after public reward experience, and how long does the reader live?
inputs: Feeder signal, energy, previous action, anonymous outgoing controls, issued bit, chosen outgoing slot and public energy bill; training is on a disjoint structural fold.
forbidden_inputs: Source, holder identities, coordinates, law as an observable signal, hidden ledger, movements not taken, tapes, scores computed using future truth, test feedback or empty status on a pass.
mapping: Four supplied route and arrival tests and a fixed local reward update in score registers, a fixed physical selector and the same action mark at every query.
primary_observable: Opposite-stock errors and certificates; actual pairs and useful reciprocal second-memory flips with first memory fixed and sham and erasure; separately mean paired turns to death against both old keeper and current-only.
comparators_or_controls: No update, physically fixed strict return, re-paired training receipts, permuted selector, erased selected memory, feedback-sham, shared decision comparisons; route and order controls.
resource_budget: First 32/32/64 eligible train/mechanism/survival founders in disjoint structural folds; 8/16/8 tapes, all founder funds and stalls; 56 imposed prefixes in the mechanism fold; two laws. No early survival censoring.
first_executable_signal: Recover the previous equal-exit alias cases, validate the independent design, and check the local transition on earlier or synthetic public records.
stop_rule: Conclude for the frozen policy class when the three questions have separate per-law answers including all ambiguity, controls and seed replay; native creation of the supplied apparatus is outside this finite experiment.
nonclaims: Exploratory finite evidence; the externally supplied cue repertoire, credit, game, readout and preparation are fixed choices. No assumption of general map knowledge or a better survival policy until scored.
